initiate_delegated_session.title: Initiate Delegated Session

keep_session_alive.title: Session Keep Alive

add_document_to_binder.title: Add Document to Binder
add_document_to_binder.description: Add a document to a binder. Binders cannot exceed 50,000 nodes. Nodes include documents, sections, and component binders. If a binder has reached its limit, binder nodes cannot be added to the binder or any of its component binders, even if the component binders have not reached the 50,000 node limit.

document_id_v.description: ID of the document being added to the binder.

parent_id_v.description: Section ID of the parent section, if the document will be in a section rather than top-level. Note: the section ID is unique no matter where it is in the binder hierarchy. Blank means adding the document at the top-level binder.

order_v.description: Enter a number reflecting the position of the document within the binder or section. A value of `1` has special behavior and instructs Vault to place the document at the first ordinal position of the binder, regardless of any existing `order__v` values. If provided with a negative value or omitted, Vault places the document at the last ordinal position of the binder, regardless of any existing `order__v` values.

binding_rule_v.description: The binding rule indicating which version of the document will be linked to the binder and the ongoing behavior. Options are: `default` (bind to the latest available version (assumed if binding\_rule is blank)), `steady-state` (bind to latest version in a steady-state), `current` (bind to current version), or `specific` (bind to a specific version).

major_version_number_v.description: If `binding_rule__v=specific`, then this is required and indicates the major version of the document to be linked. Otherwise it is ignored.

minor_version_number_v.description: If `binding_rule__v=specific`, then this is required and indicates the minor version of the document to be linked. Otherwise it is ignored.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

attachments.description: To export binder attachments, include the parameter `attachments=all` to export all versions of all attachments or `attachments=latest` to export the latest version of all attachments.

docfield.description: Set to `false` to exclude document metadata from the export. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and the export will include document metadata.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the binder export job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the binder export request.

export_binder.title: Export Binder
export_binder.description: Use this request to export the latest version of a binder in your Vault. This request exports the complete binder, including all binder sections, document metadata, and source files. The version binding rule configured for the binder, section, or binder document determines which document versions are exported. Learn more about exporting binders in Vault Help.

source.description: Set to `false` to exclude source files from the export. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and the export will include source files.

renditiontype.description: To include renditions in the export, add the parameter `renditiontype={rendition_type}` to the request endpoint. Rendition types may vary depending on your Vault’s configuration. Valid rendition types include: `viewable_rendition__v`; `imported_rendition__c`; `audio_rendition__v`; `unmodified_source__sys`

name.description: To define a document naming rule, which is the document field to use for naming exported files, add the parameter `name={field}` to the request endpoint. If omitted, defaults to `name__v`. Valid document field values include: `name__v`; `document_number__v`; `export_filename__v`; `title__v`

docversion.description: To override the binding rule and export all major versions of each document in the binder, add the parameter `docversion=major` to the request endpoint. To override the binding rule and export all major and minor versions of each document, add the parameter `docversion=major_minor` to the request endpoint.

attachments.description: To export binder attachments, include the parameter `attachments=all` to export all versions of all attachments or `attachments=latest` to export the latest version of all attachments.

docfield.description: Set to `false` to exclude document metadata from the export. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and the export will include document metadata.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the binder export job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the binder export request.

get_binder_export_results.title: Retrieve Binder Export Results
get_binder_export_results.description: After submitting a request to export a binder from your Vault, you can query Vault to determine the results of the request. Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested a binder export job (via the API) which is no longer active. You must have a valid `job_id` value (retrieved from the export binder request).

job_id.description: The `id` value of the requested export job. This is returned with the export binder requests above.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `job_id` | The Job ID value of the binder export request. | | `id` | The `id` value of the exported binder.

list_binder_versions.title: Retrieve All Binder Versions
list_binder_versions.description: Retrieve All Binder Versions. Retrieve all versions of a binder.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Binders have versions just like regular documents. On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns a list of the available versions for the specified binder.

get_binder_version.title: Retrieve Binder Version
get_binder_version.description: Retrieve the fields and values configured on a specific version of a specific binder.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns the binder contents, fields, and values configured on the binder, including the first level of nodes in the binder’s structure.

get_binder.title: Retrieve Binder
get_binder.description: Retrieve all fields and values configured on a specific binder in your Vault. By default, this endpoint retrieves the first level (root) of the binder's structure. To retrieve all levels, use the `depth` query parameter. For binders with unbound documents, this endpoint retrieves versions based on binder display options for unbound documents set in the Vault UI. Learn more about document type settings in Vault Help. To retrieve a list of all binders in your Vault, we recommend using Direct Data API or VQL (`SELECT id FROM binders`).

depth.description: To retrieve all information in all levels of the binder, set this to `all`. If omitted, defaults to retrieving information for only the first level.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault retrieves the fields and components of the binder in a hierarchical structure, showing the parent-child relationships for each item and maintaining the specific order of the objects in each level.

reclassify_binder.title: Reclassify Binder
reclassify_binder.description: Reclassify allows you to change the document type of an existing binder. A document "type" is the combination of the `type__v`, `subtype__v`, and `classification__v` fields on a binder. When you reclassify, Vault may add or remove certain fields on the binder. You can only reclassify the latest version of a binder and only one binder at a time. The API does not currently support Bulk Reclassify. Learn more about: Vault Help: Reclassifying Documents. API: Retrieve Binders API: Retrieve Document Fields API: Retrieve Document Types, Subtypes, and Classifications

reclassify.description: Set to `true`. Without this, a standard binder update action is performed.

type_v.description: The name of the document type being assigned to the binder.

subtype_v.description: The name of the document subtype (if one exists on the type).

classification_v.description: The name of the document classification (if one exists on the subtype).

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

refresh_binder_auto_filing.title: Refresh Binder Auto-Filing
refresh_binder_auto_filing.description: Refresh Binder Auto-Filing. Calls POST /api/{version}/objects/binders/{binder_id}/actions on the Vault API.

action_refresh_auto_filing.description: Trigger auto-filing for a specific binder. This is analogous to the Refresh Auto-Filing action in the UI.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

update_binder_version.title: Update Binder Version
update_binder_version.description: Update Binder Version. Calls PUT /api/{version}/objects/binders/{binder_id}/versions/{major_version}/{minor_version} on the Vault API.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. In the body of the request, add any editable field values that you wish to update. To remove existing field values, include the field name and set its value to null. To find these fields, Retrieve Binder Version configured on binders.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault updates field values for the specified version of the binder and returns the ID of the updated binder.

update_binder.title: Update Binder
update_binder.description: Update editable field values on the latest version of a single binder.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. In the body of the request, add any editable field values that you wish to update as name-value pairs. To remove existing field values, include the field name and set its value to null. To find these fields for the specific binder, use Retrieve Binder.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault updates field values for the latest version of the binder and returns the ID of the updated binder.

export_bulk_translation_file.title: Export Bulk Translation File
export_bulk_translation_file.description: Export a bulk translation file from your Vault. The exported bulk translation file is a CSV editable in any text editor or translation software. You can request one (1) message type in one (1) language per request. Learn more about the translation file schema in Vault Help. This request starts an asynchronous job that exports the translation file to your Vault's file staging. You can then download this file with the Download Item Content request. You must have the Admin: Language: Read permission to export a bulk translation file from Vault.

lang.description: A valid language code value, for example, `en`. Retrieve available values from the Admin Key (`admin_key__sys`) field on the Language (`language__sys`) object. Active and Inactive languages are both valid.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `url` and `job_id` of the job. You can use this to retrieve the status and results of the request. When the job is complete, the translation files are available on your Vault's file staging.

export_label_set.title: Export Label Set
export_label_set.description: Export a Label Set file from your Vault. The exported Label Set file is a CSV editable in any text editor or translation software. You can request one (1) message type in one (1) Label Set per request. Learn more about the Label Set file schema in Vault Help. This request starts an asynchronous job that exports the Label Set file to your Vault’s file staging. You can then download this file with the Download Item Content request or Vault Toolbox. To import a Label Set, use the Import Bulk Translation File request and set the `message_type` to `field_labels__sys`.

message_type.description: The message type name, which must be `field_labels__sys`.

name.description: A valid Label Set, for example, `medical_english__c`. Active and Inactive Label Sets are both valid.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `url` and `job_id` of the job. You can use this to retrieve the status and results of the request. When the job is complete, the Label Set file is available on your Vault’s file staging.

import_bulk_translation_files.title: Import Bulk Translation Files
import_bulk_translation_files.description: Import bulk translation files into Vault. While an exported bulk translation file can contain only one (1) language, your import file may include multiple languages. Vault reads the language value separately for each row and applies any new translations immediately. Vault ignores any rows without changes. Learn more about the translation file schema in Vault Help. You must have the Admin: Language: Edit permission to import a bulk translation file to Vault. Upload the CSV file to your Vault’s file staging before making this request. The maximum CSV input file size is 1GB. The values in the input must be UTF-16 encoded and tab-delimited.

file_paths.description: A comma-separated list of the file paths of the CSV files on file staging. Cannot contain `./` or any other path traversal directives. If any of the provided filenames are invalid, the entire request fails to send.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `job_id` which allows you to: Retrieve the job status, which specifies if the import job has completed with `SUCCESS` Retrieve the job summary, which provides details of a successful job Retrieve the job errors, which pr…

get_import_bulk_translation_file_job_err.title: Retrieve Import Bulk Translation File Job Errors
get_import_bulk_translation_file_job_err.description: After submitting a request to import bulk translation files, you can query Vault to determine the errors from the request (if any). Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested an Import Bulk Translation Files job (via Vault API) which is no longer active You must be the user who initiated the job or have the Admin: Jobs: Read permission

job_id.description: The `id` value of the requested import job. This was returned from the Import Bulk Translation File request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the line number and error message for any errors encountered in the job.

get_import_bulk_translation_file_job_sum.title: Retrieve Import Bulk Translation File Job Summary
get_import_bulk_translation_file_job_sum.description: After submitting a request to import a bulk translation file, you can query Vault to determine the results of the request. Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested an Import Bulk Translation File job (via the API) which is no longer active You must be the user who initiated the job or have the Admin: Jobs: Read permission

job_id.description: The `id` value of the requested import job. This was returned from the Import Bulk Translation File request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following `data`: `ignored`: The number of rows that were ignored. For example, Vault ignores any rows without changes. `updated`: The number of existing rows that were updated successfully.

query_component_definitions.title: Component Definition Query
query_component_definitions.description: Retrieve MDL definitions (`mdl_definition__v`) and JSON definitions (`json_definition__v`) of Vault components using a VQL query on the `vault_component__v` and `vault_package_component__v` query targets. Learn more in the VQL documentation.

record_properties.description: Optional: If present, the response includes the record properties object. Possible values are `all`, `hidden`, `redacted`, and `weblink`. If omitted, the record properties object is not included in the response. Learn more.

q.description: A VQL query on the `vault_component__v` or `vault_package_component__v` query targets. The query can be up to 50,000 characters, formatted as `q={query}`. For example, `q=SELECT id FROM vault_component__v`. Note that submitting the query as a query parameter instead may cause you to exceed the maximum URL length.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `pagesize` | The number of records displayed per page. This can be modified. Learn more.

deploy_package.title: Deploy Package
deploy_package.description: Deploy Package. Calls POST /api/{version}/vobject/vault_package__v/{package_id}/actions/deploy on the Vault API.

package_id.description: The `id` field value of the `vault_package__v` object record used for deployment. See Import Package.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the export job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the request.

disable_configuration_mode.title: Disable Configuration Mode
disable_configuration_mode.description: Disable Configuration Mode in the currently authenticated Vault. When you disable Configuration Mode, non-Admin users can now access the Vault. Learn more about Configuration Mode in Vault Help.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, this endpoint disables Configuration Mode in the currently authenticated Vault. Vault allows non-Admin users to log back in.

enable_configuration_mode.title: Enable Configuration Mode
enable_configuration_mode.description: Enable Configuration Mode in the currently authenticated Vault. When enabled, Configuration Mode locks non-Admin users out of the Vault. Vault Owners and System Admins can still access the Vault to deploy configuration migration packages or set up Dynamic Access Control (DAC). Users with access to multiple Vaults can log in if at least one (1) Vault in the domain is not in Configuration Mode. Learn more about Configuration Mode in Vault Help.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, this endpoint enables Configuration Mode in the currently authenticated Vault, terminates sessions for any non-Admin users currently logged in, and prevents other non-Admin users from logging in.

export_package.title: Export Package
export_package.description: Export Package. Calls POST /api/{version}/services/package on the Vault API.

package_name.description: The name of the Outbound Package you would like to export.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the export job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the request.

import_package.title: Import Package
import_package.description: Asynchronously import and validate a VPK package attached to this request. On completion, Vault sends an email notification which includes a link to the validation log. For packages that include Vault Java SDK code, this checks code compilation and restrictions in use of the JDK. For example, `new` is not allowed for non-allowlisted classes. Learn more about Vault Java SDK limits and restrictions.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the import job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the request.

get_outbound_package_dependencies.title: Retrieve Outbound Package Dependencies
get_outbound_package_dependencies.description: Outbound packages only include configuration details for the included components. Sometimes, a configuration for one component depends on another component or subcomponent which you may not have explicitly specified. With this API, you can retrieve all outstanding component dependencies for an outbound package, including references to sub-components. This request returns up to 3 levels of dependencies and up to 2,000 unique dependencies. You can then add these missing dependencies to the package with the Create Object Records API.

package_id.description: The ID of the `outbound_package__v` record from which to retrieve dependencies.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `total_dependencies` | The total number of outstanding component dependencies. | | `target_vault_id` | The ID of the target Vault for the outbound package.

get_package_deploy_results.title: Retrieve Package Deploy Results
get_package_deploy_results.description: After Vault has finished processing the deploy job, use this request to retrieve the results of the completed deployment.

package_id.description: The `id` field value of the `vault_package__v` object record used for deployment. See Deploy Package.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The `deployment_log` provides a URL to download the latest version of the deployment log. If the deployed package includes datasets, the response also provides the `data_deployment_log` with a URL to download the data deployment log.

validate_inbound_package.title: Validate Inbound Package
validate_inbound_package.description: Validate an imported VPK package before deploying it to your Vault. The validation response includes information on dependent components and whether they exist in the package or in your Vault. You can then add missing dependencies to the package in the source Vault before re-importing and deploying it to your target Vault. Learn more about validation logs in Vault Help.

package_id.description: The `id` field value of the `vault_package__v` object record to validate.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

validate_package.title: Validate Package
validate_package.description: Validate a VPK package attached to this request. The validation response will include the same information on dependent components as validation logs generated through the UI. For packages that include Vault Java SDK code, this operation recompiles source code against the target Vault's libraries and dependencies and checks for compilation errors and restrictions. For example, `new` is not allowed for non-allowlisted classes. When compilation errors are detected, Vault assigns the code step a status of Blocked. Learn more about Vault Java SDK limits and restrictions. This endpoint does not import your package.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. To upload the VPK file, use the multi-part attachment with the file component `”file={filename}”`. The maximum allowed file size is 2GB.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information about the VPK package: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `summary` | The summary of the package. | | `author` | The user who created the package.

run_vault_compare.title: Vault Compare
run_vault_compare.description: Compare the configuration of two different Vaults. The Vault you make the request in is the source Vault, and the target Vault for the comparison is listed in the body. Learn more about Vault Compare in Vault Help. The user who makes the request must be a cross-domain user and must have access to the `vault_component__v` in both Vaults. Learn more about cross-domain users in Vault Help.

vault_id.description: The target Vault `id` for the comparison.

results_type.description: To include all configuration values, set this to `complete`. To only see the differences between Vaults, set to `differences`. If omitted, this defaults to `differences`.

details_type.description: To show component level details only, set to `none`. To include simple attribute-level details, set to `simple`. To show all attribute-level details, set to `complex`. If omitted, this defaults to `simple`.

include_doc_binder_templates.description: To exclude Document and Binder Templates for comparison, set to `false`. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and templates are included.

include_vault_settings.description: To exclude Vault Settings for comparison, set to `false`. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and Vault Settings are included.

component_types.description: Add a comma separated list of component types to include. For example, `Doclifecycle, Doctype, Workflow`. To exclude all component types, set to `none`. If omitted, this defaults to include all components.

generate_outbound_packages.description: If set to `true`, Vault automatically generates an Outbound Package based on differences between the source Vault and target Vault. If omitted, the default value is `false`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `url` and `job_id` of the new Comparison Report job. You can use these to find the Job Status, and using the links from the job status response, download your report. The download is an Excel file.

run_vault_configuration_report.title: Vault Configuration Report
run_vault_configuration_report.description: Generate an Excel report containing configuration information for a Vault. Users must have the Vault Configuration Report permission to use this API.

include_vault_settings.description: To exclude Vault Settings for comparison, set to `false`. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and Vault Settings are included.

include_inactive_components.description: If set to `true`, inactive components and subcomponents are included in the report. If omitted, defaults to `false` and only active components and subcomponents are included. See details for inactive workflows.

include_components_modified_since.description: Only include components modified since the specified date. Provide the date in the format `yyyy-mm-dd`. If omitted, includes all components. This option is not available for subcomponents.

include_doc_binder_templates.description: To exclude document and binder templates, set to `false`. If omitted, this defaults to `true` and document and binder templates are included.

suppress_empty_results.description: If set to `true`, Vault excludes tabs with only header rows from the report.

component_types.description: Add a comma-separated list of component types to include. For example, `Doclifecycle,Doctype,Workflow`. If omitted, this defaults to include all components and Vault includes an Excel object data report in the ZIP file output.

output_format.description: Output report as either an `Excel` (XSLX) or `Excel_Macro_Enabled` (XLSM) file. If omitted, defaults to `Excel_Macro_Enabled`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `url` and `job_id` of the new Configuration Report job. You can use these to find the Job Status, and using the link from the job status response, download your report. The download is a ZIP file.

delete_single_client_code_distribution.title: Delete Single Client Code Distribution
delete_single_client_code_distribution.description: Delete a specific client code distribution. To delete a distribution, you must first remove all `Page` components associated with it from your Vault. To delete a single file from an existing distribution, re-package the distribution without the file and re-upload the distribution to Vault.

distribution_name.description: The `name` attribute of the client code distribution to delete.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

download_single_client_code_distribution.title: Download Single Client Code Distribution
download_single_client_code_distribution.description: Download a ZIP file containing the client code distribution directory, including the client code files and the distribution manifest (`distribution-manifest.json`).

distribution_name.description: The `name` attribute of the client code distribution to download.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

list_client_code_distribution_metadata.title: Retrieve All Client Code Distribution Metadata
list_client_code_distribution_metadata.description: Retrieves a list of all client code distributions in the Vault and their metadata. This endpoint does not retrieve the contents of distribution manifest files.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The response lists all client code distributions in the Vault and the following metadata for each distribution: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The name of the client code distribution.

get_single_client_code_distribution_meta.title: Retrieve Single Client Code Distribution Metadata
get_single_client_code_distribution_meta.description: Retrieve metadata for a specific client code distribution, including its name, size, and details from the uploaded `distribution-manifest.json` file.

distribution_name.description: The `name` attribute of the client code distribution to retrieve.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The response contains the following metadata, including metadata provided in the `distribution-manifest.json` file: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The name of the client code distribution.

download_direct_data_file.title: Download Direct Data File
download_direct_data_file.description: Download Direct Data File. Download a Direct Data file. Calls GET /api/{version}/services/directdata/files/{name} on the Vault API.

name.description: The `name` of the Direct Data file part. Obtain this from the Retrieve Available Direct Data Files request. For example, `146478-20240213-0000-F.001`.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

get_available_direct_data_files.title: Retrieve Available Direct Data Files
get_available_direct_data_files.description: Retrieve a list of all Direct Data files available for download.

extract_type.description: The Direct Data file type: `incremental_directdata`, `full_directdata`, or `log_directdata`. If omitted, returns all files. Learn more about Direct Data file types.

start_time.description: Specify a time in `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format. For example, 7AM on January 15, 2024 would use `2024-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the Vault’s creation date and time. All Full files have a start time of `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

stop_time.description: Specify a time in `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format. For example, 9AM on January 15, 2024 would use `2024-01-15T09:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to today’s date and current time.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault lists all Direct Data files available for download. The response includes the following metadata for each file that is published: | Metadata Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The name of the Direct Data file, excluding the.gzip…

assign_users_groups_to_roles_on_single_b.title: Assign Users & Groups to Roles on a Single Binder
assign_users_groups_to_roles_on_single_b.description: Assign Users & Groups to Roles on a Single Binder. Assign users and groups to roles on a single binder.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `{role__v}.users` | A string of comma-separated user id values for the new role. For example, `reviewer__v.users = "3003, 4005"`. | | `{role__v}.groups` | A string of comma-separated group id values for the new group. For example, `reviewer__v.groups = "20, 21"`. |

remove_users_groups_from_roles_on_single.title: Remove Users & Groups from Roles on a Single Binder

create_document_tokens.description: The Vault Document Tokens API allows you to generate document access tokens needed by the external viewer to view documents outside of Vault. Learn more.

doc_ids.description: Include the `docIds` request parameter with a comma-separated string of document `id` values. This will generate tokens for each document. For example: `docIds=101,102,103,104`

expiry_date_offset.description: Include the `expiryDateOffset` request parameter set to the number of days after which the tokens will expire and the documents will no longer be available in the viewer. If not specified, the tokens will expire after 10 years by default.

download_option.description: Include the `downloadOption` request parameter set to `PDF`, `source`, `both`, or `none`. These allow users viewing the document to be able to download a PDF version or source version (Word, PowerPoint, etc.) of the document. If not specified, the download options default to those set on each document.

channel.description: Include the `channel` request parameter set to the website object record `id` value that corresponds to the distribution channel where the document is being made available. If no website record is specified, Vault will assume the request is for Approved Email.

token_group.description: Include the `tokenGroup` request parameter to group together generated tokens for multiple documents in order to display the documents being referenced in the same viewer. This value accepts strings of alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and single consecutive underscores) up to 255 characters in length. The token that is passed as a URL parameter to the External Viewer is the primary token and the document it references will be displayed normally.

steady_state.description: If set to `true`, Vault generates a token for the latest steady state version of a document. If you do not have View permission, or if a steady-state version does not exist, Vault returns an `INVALID_STATE` error. If omitted, the default value is `false`, and Vault generates a token for the latest version, regardless of state.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns a list of all available versions of the specified document. In the example response, document `id:534` has 8 different versions. Version 2.0 is the latest steady state version. Version 2.3 is the latest version.

get_document.title: Retrieve Document
get_document.description: Retrieve Document. Retrieve all metadata from a document. Calls GET /api/{version}/objects/documents/{doc_id} on the Vault API.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The boolean field `binder__v` indicates whether the returned document is a regular document (`true`) or a binder (`false`). The absence of this field means it is a document.

create_multiple_document_versions.title: Create Multiple Document Versions
create_multiple_document_versions.description: Create or add document versions in bulk. The maximum CSV input file size is 1GB. The values in the input must be UTF-8 encoded. CSVs must follow the standard RFC 4180 format, with some exceptions. The maximum batch size is 500.

id_param.description: If you're identifying documents in your input by a unique field, add `idParam={fieldname}` to the request endpoint. You can use any object field which has `unique` set to `true` in the object metadata, with the exception of picklists. For example, `idParam=external_id__v`.

migration_mode.description: Must be set to `true`. Vault allows you to manually set the name and version number and to create documents in any lifecycle state using the `status__v` field, but does not allow you to change the document number. Vault also bypasses entry criteria, entry actions, and event actions and does not send notifications. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

csv.description: The request body as CSV text, with a header row. Columns: file (required): The filepath of your source file. The maximum allowed file size is 500GB.; id: The system-assigned document ID of the document to add the versions to.; external_id__v: Instead of `id`, you can use this user-defined document external ID.; name__v (required): Enter a name for the new document. This may be the same name as the existing document/version or a different n…; type__v (required): Enter the name or label of the document type to assign to the new document.; subtype__v: Enter the name or label of the document subtype (if one exists on the document type).; classification__v: Enter the name or label of the document classification (if one exists on the document subtype).; lifecycle__v (required): Enter the name or label of the document lifecycle to assign to the new document.; major_version_number__v (required):…

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

reclassify_multiple_documents.title: Reclassify Multiple Documents
reclassify_multiple_documents.description: Reclassify documents in bulk. Reclassify allows you to change the document type of existing documents or assign document types to unclassified documents. A document "type" is the combination of the `type__v`, `subtype__v`, and `classification__v` fields on a document. When you reclassify, Vault may add or remove certain fields on the document. Not all documents are eligible for reclassification. For example, you can only reclassify the latest version of a document and you cannot reclassify a checked out document. Learn more about reclassifying documents in Vault Help. The maximum CSV input file size is 1GB.

migration_mode.description: When set to `true`, Vault allows you to manually set the document number and to update documents to any lifecycle state using the `status__v` field. Vault does not send notifications in Document Migration Mode. All other Document Migration Mode overrides available at document creation are ignored, but do not generate an error message. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

csv.description: The request body as CSV text, with a header row. Columns: id (required): The ID of the document to reclassify.; lifecycle__v (required): The name of the document lifecycle. When assigning a document type to an unclassified document, you must provi…; type__v (required): The name of the document type.; subtype__v: The name of the document subtype (if one exists on the type).; classification__v: The name of the document classification (if one exists on the subtype).; document_number__v: The document number for the reclassified document. If omitted, the document retains the existing document numb…; status__v: Specifies the document lifecycle state for the reclassified document.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns the IDs of the reclassified documents.

reclassify_single_document.title: Reclassify Single Document
reclassify_single_document.description: Reclassify allows you to change the document type of an existing document or assign a document type to an unclassified document. This endpoint is analogous to the Reclassify action in the Vault UI. A document "type" is the combination of the `type__v`, `subtype__v`, and `classification__v` fields on a document. When you reclassify, Vault may add or remove certain fields on the document. Add these new fields and values to the body of this request. If a new required field is missing, the error response will list the name of the required field. To reclassify more than one document, use the Reclassify Multiple Documents endpoint.

migration_mode.description: When set to `true`, Vault allows you to manually set the document number and to update documents to any lifecycle state using the `status__v` field. Vault does not send notifications in Document Migration Mode. All other Document Migration Mode overrides available at document creation are ignored, but do not generate an error message. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

type_v.description: The name of the document type.

subtype_v.description: The name of the document subtype (if one exists on the type).

classification_v.description: The name of the document classification (if one exists on the subtype).

lifecycle_v.description: The name of the document lifecycle. When assigning a document type to an unclassified document, you must provide Inbox (`unclassified__v`) as the lifecycle to bypass required field validation.

reclassify.description: Set to `true`. Without this, a standard document update action is performed.

document_number_v.description: The document number for the reclassified document. If omitted, the document retains the existing document number. You must set both the `reclassify` parameter and the `X-VaultAPI_MigrationMode` header to `true` to change the document number, and you can only include this parameter when you also change the document lifecycle or type, subtype, or classification.

status_v.description: Specifies the document lifecycle state for the reclassified document. If omitted, the document retains the existing state. You must set both the `reclassify` parameter and the `X-VaultAPI_MigrationMode` header to `true` to change the state, and you can only include this parameter when you also change the document lifecycle or type, subtype, or classification.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns the ID of the reclassified document.

update_document_version.title: Update Document Version
update_document_version.description: Update editable field values on a specific version of a document. See also Update Single Document.

migration_mode.description: When set to `true`, Vault allows you to manually set the document number. Vault does not send notifications in Document Migration Mode. All other Document Migration Mode overrides available at document creation are ignored, but do not generate an error message. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. In the body of the request, add any editable field values that you wish to update as name-value pairs. To remove existing field values, include the field name and set its value to null. To find your Vault’s editable document fields, Retrieve All Document Fields configured on documents. Editable fields will have `editable:true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault updates field values for the specified version of the document and returns the ID of the updated document.

update_multiple_documents.title: Update Multiple Documents
update_multiple_documents.description: Bulk update editable field values on multiple documents. You can only update the latest version of each document. To update past document versions, see Update Document Version. The maximum CSV input file size is 1GB. The values in the input must be UTF-8 encoded. CSVs must follow the standard RFC 4180 format, with some exceptions. The maximum batch size is 1,000.

migration_mode.description: When set to `true`, Vault allows you to change the document number. Vault does not send notifications in Document Migration Mode. All other Document Migration Mode overrides available at document creation are ignored, but do not generate an error message. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

id.description: Conditional. The ID of the document to update. Only required when uploading a CSV file.

doc_ids.description: Conditional. Comma-separated list of the IDs of documents to update. Only required when entering key-value pairs in the body of your request.

archive_v.description: To archive a document, set to `true`. To unarchive a document, set to `false`. The default is `false`. Document archive is not available in all Vaults. Learn more in Vault Help.

template_doctype_v.description: If you need to create a controlled document template from this document, enter a value for the Template Document Type field. To retrieve a list of all possible field values for this field, Retrieve the Object Collection for `doc_type_detail__v`. Learn more about controlled document template creation in Vault Help.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

update_single_document.title: Update Single Document
update_single_document.description: Update editable field values on the latest version of a single document. To update past document versions, see Update Document Version. Note that this endpoint does not allow you to update the `archive__v` field. To archive a document, or to update multiple documents at once, see Update Multiple Documents.

migration_mode.description: When set to `true`, Vault allows you to change the document number. Vault does not send notifications in Document Migration Mode. All other Document Migration Mode overrides available at document creation are ignored, but do not generate an error message. You must have the Document Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Document Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Document Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, and custom doctype triggers.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. In the body of the request, add any editable field values that you wish to update. To find these fields, Retrieve Document Fields configured on documents. Editable fields will have `editable:true`. To remove existing field values, include the field name and set its value to null.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault updates field values for the latest version of the document and returns the ID of the updated document.

get_domain_information.title: Retrieve Domain Information
get_domain_information.description: Domain Admins can use this request to retrieve a list of all Vaults currently in their domain.

include_application.description: To include Vault application type information in the response, set `include_application` to `true`. If omitted, defaults to `false` and application information is not included.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `domain_name__v` | The name of the domain containing the Vaults. This is unique to each customer and part of the DNS of each Vault. | | `domain_type__v` | The type of domain (Production, Sandbox, Demo, or Test).

get_domains.title: Retrieve Domains
get_domains.description: Non-domain Admins can use this request to retrieve a list of all their domains, including the domain of the current Vault. You can use this data as a valid `domain` value when creating a sandbox Vault.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

add_edl_matched_documents.title: Add EDL Matched Documents
add_edl_matched_documents.description: Add matched documents to EDL Items. You must have a security profile that grants the Application: EDL Matching: Edit Document Matches permission, and EDL Matched Document APIs must be enabled in your Vault. To enable this feature, contact Veeva Support.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: id (required): The EDL Item `id` to match to documents. EDL Item records and their parent records must have a `status__v` of…; document_id (required): The document `id` to match to an EDL Item.; major_version_number__v: The major version number of a document. You must also include `minor_version_number__v` to use this parameter.; minor_version_number__v: The minor version number of a document. You must also include `major_version_number__v` to use this parameter.; lock: If set to `true`, locks the EDL Item to match a specific steady state document version or, if version numbers…

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes a `SUCCESS` or `FAILURE` status and any applicable error messages for each EDL Item to document match in the body of your request.

bulk_update_edl_node_order.title: Bulk Update Node Order
bulk_update_edl_node_order.description: Given multiple EDL parent nodes, update the order of each set of children.

object_name.description: The name of the corresponding hierarchy-enabled object for which to update the node order in bulk. For example, `edl__v`, `edl_item__v`, or `edl_template__v`.

id_param.description: To identify nodes in your input by a unique field on the corresponding record, add `idParam={field_name}` to the request endpoint. You can use any record field that has `unique` set to `true` in the record metadata. For example, `idParam=external_id__v`. If `idParam` is included, `parent_id` and `id` are not required in the request body.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: parent_id: The parent node ID from the `veeva_hierarchy_node` table. Not required if `idParam` is included.; id: The node ID from the `veeva_hierarchy_node` table. Not required if `idParam` is included.; order__v (required): An integer specifying the sibling ordering.
