output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

create_placeholder_from_edl_item.title: Create a Placeholder from an EDL Item
create_placeholder_from_edl_item.description: Create a placeholder from an EDL item. Learn about working with Content Placeholders in Vault Help.

edl_item_ids.description: Comma separated list of EDL Item ids on which to initiate the action.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: `url` - The URL to retrieve the current status of the export job. `job_id` - The Job ID value is used to retrieve the status and results of the request.

remove_edl_matched_documents.title: Remove EDL Matched Documents
remove_edl_matched_documents.description: Remove manually matched documents from EDL Items. You must have a security profile that grants the Application: EDL Matching: Edit Document Matches permission, and EDL Matched Document APIs must be enabled in your Vault. To enable this feature, contact Veeva Support.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: id (required): The EDL Item `id` to match to documents. EDL Item records and their parent records must have a `status__v` of…; document_id (required): The document `id` to match to an EDL Item.; major_version_number__v: The major version number of a document. You must also include `minor_version_number__v` to use this parameter.; minor_version_number__v: The minor version number of a document. You must also include `major_version_number__v` to use this parameter.; remove_locked: If set to `true`, removes a matched document from the EDL Item even if the EDL Item is locked to a specific st…

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes a `SUCCESS` or `FAILURE` status and any applicable error messages for each matched document to remove from an EDL Item in the body of your request.

get_edl_node_children.title: Retrieve a Node's Children
get_edl_node_children.description: Given an EDL node ID, retrieves immediate children (not grandchildren) of that node. Learn more about EDL hierarchies in Vault Help.

edl_hierarchy_or_template.description: Choose to retrieve node children for either `edl_hierarchy__v` or `edl_template__v`.

parent_node_id.description: The ID of a parent node in the hierarchy.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

list_edl_root_nodes.title: Retrieve All Root Nodes
list_edl_root_nodes.description: Retrieves all root EDL nodes and node metadata. Learn more about EDL hierarchies in Vault Help.

edl_hierarchy_or_template.description: Choose to retrieve nodes for either `edl_hierarchy__v` or `edl_template__v`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_edl_root_nodes.title: Retrieve Specific Root Nodes
get_edl_root_nodes.description: Retrieve Specific Root Nodes. Retrieves the root node ID for the given EDL record IDs.

edl_hierarchy_or_template.description: Choose to retrieve nodes for either `edl_hierarchy__v` or `edl_template__v`.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: ref_id__v (required): The ID of the EDL record whose root node you’d like to retrieve. Maximum 1,000 IDs per request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

update_edl_node_order.title: Update Node Order
update_edl_node_order.description: Update Node Order. Given an EDL parent node, update the order of its children.

edl_hierarchy_or_template.description: Choose to update node order for either `edl_hierarchy__v` or `edl_template__v`.

parent_node_id.description: The ID of a parent node in the hierarchy.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: id (required): The ID of the child node to update.; order__v (required): The new order for the node in the hierarchy, such as "1", "2", etc.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

delete_file_or_folder.title: Delete File or Folder
delete_file_or_folder.description: Delete File or Folder. Delete an individual file or folder from file staging.

item.description: The absolute path to the file or folder to delete. This path is specific to the authenticated user. Admin users can access the root directory. All other users can only access their own user directory.

recursive.description: Applicable to deleting folders only. If `true`, the request will delete the contents of a folder and all subfolders. The default is `false`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `job_id` | The Job ID value to retrieve the status and results of the request. | | `url` | URL to retrieve the current job status of this request. |

download_item_content.title: Download Item Content
download_item_content.description: Retrieve the content of a specified file from file staging. Use the `Range` header to create resumable downloads for large files, or to continue downloading a file if your session is interrupted.

item.description: The absolute path to a file. This path is specific to the authenticated user. Admin users can access the root directory. All other users can only access their own user directory.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

list_items_at_path.title: List Items at a Path
list_items_at_path.description: Return a list of files and folders for the specified path. Paths are different for Admin users (Vault Owners and System Admins) and non-Admin users. Learn more about paths in the Vault API Documentation.

item.description: The absolute path to a file or folder. This path is specific to the authenticated user. Admin users can access the root directory. All other users can only access their own user directory.

recursive.description: If `true`, the response will contain the contents of all subfolders. If not specified, the default value is `false`.

limit.description: Optional: The maximum number of items per page in the response. This can be any value between 1 and 1000. If omitted, the default value is 1000.

format_result.description: If set to `csv`, the response includes a `job_id`. Use the Job ID value to retrieve the status and results of the request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `kind` | The kind of item. This can be either `file` or `folder`.

abort_upload_session.title: Abort Upload Session
abort_upload_session.description: Abort an active upload session and purge all uploaded file parts. Admin users can see and abort all upload sessions, while non-Admin users can only see and abort sessions where they are the owner.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

commit_upload_session.title: Commit Upload Session
commit_upload_session.description: Mark an upload session as complete and assemble all previously uploaded parts to create a file.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns the `job_id` for the commit. Use the Job Status API to retrieve the job results. Upon successful completion of the job, the file will be available on the staging server.

create_resumable_upload_session.title: Create Resumable Upload Session
create_resumable_upload_session.description: Initiate a multipart upload session and return an upload session ID.

path.description: The absolute path, including file name, to place the file in the staging server. This path is specific to the authenticated user. Admin users can access the root directory. All other users can only access their own user directory.

size.description: The size of the file in bytes. The maximum file size is 500GB.

overwrite.description: If set to `true`, Vault will overwrite any existing files with the same name at the specified destination.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Upon SUCCESS, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `path` | The path to the file as specified in the request. | | `id` | The upload session ID.

get_upload_session_details.title: Get Upload Session Details
get_upload_session_details.description: Retrieve the details of an active upload session. Admin users can get details for all sessions, while non-Admin users can only get details for sessions if they are the owner.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `path` | The absolute path, including file name, to place the file in the staging server. This path is specific to the authenticated user.

list_file_parts_uploaded_to_session.title: List File Parts Uploaded to Session
list_file_parts_uploaded_to_session.description: Return a list of parts uploaded in a session. You must be an Admin user or the session owner.

limit.description: Optional: The maximum number of items per page in the response. This can be any value between 1 and 1000. If omitted, the default value is 1000.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `size` and `part_number` of each file part uploaded to the session so far. If the number of parts returned exceeds 1000 or the number defined by the `limit`, Vault includes pagination links in the response.

list_upload_sessions.title: List Upload Sessions
list_upload_sessions.description: List Upload Sessions. Return a list of active upload sessions.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault lists all active upload sessions for a Vault, along with their fields and field values. Admin users will see upload sessions for the entire Vault, while non-Admin users will see their own sessions only.

update_folder_or_file.title: Update Folder or File
update_folder_or_file.description: Move or rename a folder or file on file staging. You can move and rename an item in the same request.

item.description: The absolute path to a file or folder. This path is specific to the authenticated user. Admin users can access the root directory. All other users can only access their own user directory.

parent.description: Conditional. When moving a file or folder, specifies the absolute path to the parent directory in which to place the file.

name.description: Conditional. When renaming a file or folder, specifies the new name.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `job_id` | The Job ID value to retrieve the status and results of the request. | | `url` | URL to retrieve the current job status of this request. |

create_group.title: Create Group
create_group.description: Create Group. Calls POST /api/{version}/objects/groups on the Vault API.

label_v.description: Enter a group label. Vault uses this to create the group `name__v` value.

members_v.description: Add a comma-separated list of user IDs. This manually assigns individual users to the group.

security_profiles_v.description: Add a comma-separated list of security profiles. This automatically adds all users with the security profile to the group. These are `implied_members__v`.

active_v.description: By default, the new group will be created as active. To set the group to inactive, set this value to `false`

group_description_v.description: Add a description of the group.

allow_delegation_among_members_v.description: When set to `true`, members of this group will only be allowed to delegate access to other members of the same group. You can set this field for user and system managed groups. If omitted, defaults to `false`. Learn more about Delegate Access.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

delete_group.title: Delete Group
delete_group.description: Delete a user-defined group. You cannot delete system-managed groups.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

list_groups.title: Retrieve All Groups
list_groups.description: Retrieve all groups except Auto Managed groups. You can retrieve Auto Managed groups using the Retrieve Auto Managed Groups endpoint.

include_implied.description: Optional: When `true`, the response includes the `implied_members__v` field. These users are automatically added to the group when their `security_profiles__v` are added to the group. If omitted, the response includes only the `members__v` field. These users are individually added to a group by an Admin.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_auto_managed_groups.title: Retrieve Auto Managed Groups
get_auto_managed_groups.description: Retrieve all Auto Managed groups. Learn more about Auto Managed groups in Vault Help.

limit.description: Paginate the results by specifying the maximum number of records per page in the response. This can be any value between `1` and `1000`. If omitted, defaults to `1000`.

offset.description: Paginate the results displayed per page by specifying the amount of offset from the entry returned. For example, if you are viewing the first 50 results (page 1) and want to see the next page, set this to `offset=51`. If omitted, defaults to `0`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_group_metadata.title: Retrieve Group Metadata
get_group_metadata.description: Retrieve Group Metadata. Calls GET /api/{version}/metadata/objects/groups on the Vault API.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_group.title: Retrieve Group
get_group.description: Retrieve Group. Calls GET /api/{version}/objects/groups/{group_id} on the Vault API.

include_implied.description: When `true`, the response includes the `implied_members__v` field. These users are automatically added to the group when their `security_profiles__v` are added to the group. When not used, the response includes only the `members__v` field. These users are individually added to a group by Admin.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

update_group.title: Update Group
update_group.description: Update editable group field values. Add or remove group members and security profiles.

label_v.description: Updates the label of the group.

members_v.description: Add a comma-separated list of user IDs. This manually assigns individual users to the group.

security_profiles_v.description: Add a comma-separated list of security profiles.

active_v.description: To set the group to inactive, set this value to `false`.

group_description_v.description: Updates the description of the group.

allow_delegation_among_members_v.description: When set to `true`, members of this group will only be allowed to delegate access to other members of the same group. You can set this field for user and system managed groups. If omitted, defaults to `false`. Learn more about Delegate Access.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

cancel_job.title: Cancel Job
cancel_job.description: Request to cancel up to 500 job instances. Once cancelled, the job moves to the `CANCELLED` state. Job instances must meet certain criteria to be eligible for cancellation. Learn more about jobs eligible for cancellation in Vault Help. For example, jobs in the `SCHEDULED` state can always be cancelled. You can use Vault API or VQL to retrieve the status of a job instance.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: job_id: A JSON array or CSV of each `job_id` to cancel. Maximum 500 jobs per request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault returns an individual `responseStatus` for each of the requested job instances, either `SUCCESS` or `FAILURE`. The status of each job instance is returned in the same order as the request.

get_job_histories.title: Retrieve Job Histories
get_job_histories.description: Retrieve a history of all completed jobs in the authenticated Vault. A completed job is any job which has started and finished running, including jobs which did not complete successfully. In-progress or queued jobs do not appear here.

start_date.description: Sets the date to start retrieving completed jobs, in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. For example, for 7AM on January 15, 2016, use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the first completed job.

end_date.description: Sets the date to end retrieving completed jobs, in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. For example, for 7AM on January 15, 2016, use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the current date and time.

status.description: Filter to only retrieve jobs in a certain status. Allowed values are `success`, `errors_encountered`, `failed_to_run`, `missed_schedule`, `timeout`, `completed_due_to_inactivity`, and `cancelled`. If omitted, retrieves all statuses. Learn more about job statuses in Vault Help.

limit.description: Paginate the results by specifying the maximum number of histories per page in the response. This can be any value between `1` and `200`. If omitted, defaults to `50`.

offset.description: Paginate the results displayed per page by specifying the amount of offset from the first job history returned. If omitted, defaults to `0`. If you are viewing the first 50 results (page 1) and want to see the next page, set this to `offset=50`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_job_monitors.title: Retrieve Job Monitors
get_job_monitors.description: Retrieve monitors for jobs which have not yet completed in the authenticated Vault. An uncompleted job is any job which has not finished running, such as scheduled, queued, or actively running jobs. Completed jobs do not appear here.

start_date.description: Sets the date to start retrieving uncompleted jobs, based on the date and time the job instance was created. Value must be in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. For example, for 7AM on January 15, 2016, use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the first completed job.

end_date.description: Sets the date to end retrieving uncompleted jobs, based on the date and time the job instance was created. Value must be in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. For example, for 7AM on January 15, 2016, use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the current date and time.

status.description: Filter to only retrieve jobs in a certain status. Allowed values are `scheduled`, `queued`, `running`. If omitted, retrieves all statuses.

limit.description: Paginate the results by specifying the maximum number of jobs per page in the response. This can be any value between `1` and `200`. If omitted, defaults to `50`.

offset.description: Paginate the results displayed per page by specifying the amount of offset from the first job instance returned. If omitted, defaults to `0`. If you are viewing the first 50 results (page 1) and want to see the next page, set this to `offset=50`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_job_status.title: Retrieve Job Status
get_job_status.description: After submitting a request, you can query your Vault to determine the status of the request. To do this, you must have a valid `job_id` for a job previously requested through the API. Example Jobs: Binder Export Import Submission Export Submission Create EDL Deploy Package Deep Copy Object Record Cascade Delete Object Record Export Documents

job_id.description: The ID of the job, returned from the original job request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information. All DateTime values for scheduled jobs are in the Vault time zone for the currently authenticated user. Learn more about the Vault time zone in Vault Help.

get_sdk_job_tasks.title: Retrieve SDK Job Tasks
get_sdk_job_tasks.description: Retrieve SDK Job Tasks. Retrieve the tasks associated with an SDK job.

job_id.description: The ID of the SDK job, returned from the original job request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

start_job.title: Start Job
start_job.description: Moves up a `scheduled` job instance to start immediately. Each time a user calls this API, Vault cancels the scheduled instance of the specified job for the current interval. For example, if a job is scheduled to run daily at 11PM PST, calling this API against it at 4PM PST will cause the job to not run as scheduled at 11PM PST the same day. Vault will resume running the job at 11PM PST the next day regardless of how many times this API is called before 11PM PST the previous day. This is analogous to the Start Now option in the Vault UI.

job_id.description: The ID of the scheduled job instance to start.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_complete_audit_history_for_single_do.title: Retrieve Complete Audit History for a Single Document
get_complete_audit_history_for_single_do.description: Retrieve Complete Audit History for a Single Document. Retrieve complete audit history for a single document.

doc_id.description: The document ID for which to retrieve audit history.

start_date.description: Specify a start date to retrieve audit history. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2018 would use `2018-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the Vault's creation date.

end_date.description: Specify an end date to retrieve audit history. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2018 would use `2018-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to today's date.

format_result.description: To request a CSV file of your audit history, use `csv`. The CSV file ignores the `start_date` and `end_date`.

events.description: Provide a comma-separated list of one or more audit events to retrieve their audit history. See Vault Help for a full list of document audit events. The values passed to this parameter are case sensitive. For example, `events=WorkflowCompletion,TaskAssignment`. If omitted, defaults to all audit events.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes some of the following metadata: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `action` | The name of the action performed on the document. For example, `EditDocRelationships`. | | `item` | The document number field value.

get_complete_audit_history_for_single_ob.title: Retrieve Complete Audit History for a Single Object Record
get_complete_audit_history_for_single_ob.description: Retrieve complete audit history for a single object record. Vault does not audit individual field values for newly created records. For example, the audit trail for a new Product record would only include a single entry, and the Event Description would be “Product: CholeCap created”. We recommend exporting the current record along with the audit trail to ensure a complete export of all values. When a user deletes an object record, the audit trail captures all field values.

object_name.description: The `name__v` of the object for which to retrieve audit history.

object_record_id.description: The object record ID for which to retrieve audit history.

start_date.description: Specify a start date to retrieve audit history. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2018 would use `2018-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the Vault's creation date.

end_date.description: Specify an end date to retrieve audit history. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2018 would use `2018-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to today’s date.

format_result.description: To request a CSV file of your audit history, use `csv`.

events.description: Provide a comma-separated list of one or more audit events to retrieve their audit history. See Vault Help for a full list of object audit events. The values passed to this parameter are case sensitive. For example, `events=Copy,Edit,Delete`. If omitted, defaults to all audit events.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes some of the following metadata: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `action` | The name of the action performed on the object record. | | `item` | The name of the object and record.

get_audit_details.title: Retrieve Audit Details
get_audit_details.description: Retrieve all audit details for a specific audit type. This request supports optional parameters to narrow the results to a specified date and time within the past 30 days. You can run a full audit export with the same formatting as exports you initiate in the UI once per day per audit type. To execute a full audit export, set `all_dates` to true, leave `start_date` and `end_date` blank, and set `format_result` to `csv`. When the job is complete, you will receive an email containing links to a zipped file for each year.

audit_trail_type.description: The name of the specified audit type (`document_audit_trail`, `object_audit_trail`, etc.). Use the Retrieve Audit Types API to retrieve types available in your Vault. Requests for `login_audit_trail` only accept one request per user at a time.

start_date.description: Specify a start date to retrieve audit information. This date cannot be more than 30 days ago. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2016 would use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the start of the previous day.

end_date.description: Specify an end date to retrieve audit information. This date cannot be more than 30 days ago. Dates must be `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format, for example, 7AM on January 15, 2016 would use `2016-01-15T07:00:00Z`. If omitted, defaults to the current date and time.

all_dates.description: Set to `true` to request audit information for all dates. You must leave `start_date` and `end_date` blank when requesting an export of a full audit trail. You can only run a full audit export (`all_dates = true`) on each audit type once every 24 hours.

format_result.description: To request a downloadable CSV file of your audit details, use `csv`. The response contains a `jobId` to retrieve the job status, which contains a link to download the CSV file. If omitted, the API returns a JSON response and does not start a job. If `all_dates` is `true`, this parameter is required.

objects.description: This is an optional parameter when specifying `object_audit_trail` as the `{audit_trail_type}`. Provide a comma-separated list of one or more object names to retrieve their audit details. For example, `objects=product__v,country__v`. If omitted, defaults to all objects.

events.description: This is an optional parameter when specifying `object_audit_trail` or `document_audit_trail` as the `{audit_trail_type}`. Provide a comma-separated list of one or more audit events to retrieve their audit details. For example, `events=Edit,Delete,TaskAssignment`. If omitted, defaults to all audit events. See Vault Help for full lists of object audit events and document audit events.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all rows and fields for the specified audit trail type. For example: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `id` | The unique audit trail ID. | | `timestamp` | Date and time that the action was performed.

get_audit_metadata.description: Retrieve all fields and their metadata for a specified audit trail or log type.

audit_trail_type.description: The name of the specified audit type (`document_audit_trail`, `object_audit_trail`, etc).

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_audit_types.description: Retrieve all available audit types you have permission to access.

download_daily_api_usage.title: Download Daily API Usage
download_daily_api_usage.description: Retrieve the API Usage Log for a single day, up to 30 days in the past. The log contains information such as user name, user ID, remaining burst limit, and the endpoint called. Users with the Admin: Logs: API Usage Logs permission can access these logs. Note that the daily logs may have a delay of about 15 minutes. If your log does not include appropriate data, know that your data is not lost; it is just not yet populated. The logs are designed for troubleshooting burst limits and discovering which of your integrations are causing you to hit the limit.

date.description: The day to retrieve the API Usage log. Date is in UTC and follows the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. Date cannot be more than 30 days in the past.

log_format.description: Optional: Specify the format to download. Possible values are `csv` or `logfile`. If omitted, defaults to `csv`. Note that this call always downloads a ZIP file. This parameter only changes the format of the file contained within the ZIP.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

download_sdk_runtime_log.title: Download SDK Runtime Log
download_sdk_runtime_log.description: Retrieve the Runtime Log for a single day, up to 30 days in the past. Users with the Admin: Logs: Vault Java SDK Logs permission can access these logs. The runtime logs create entries 15 minutes after the Vault Java SDK transaction completes. If you’ve recently encountered an error which is not captured in the runtime log, wait for the transaction to finish and check again. If your log does not include appropriate data, know that your data is not lost; it is just not yet populated. Learn more about the Vault Java SDK runtime log.

date.description: The day to retrieve the runtime log. Date is in UTC and follows the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. Date cannot be more than 30 days in the past.

log_format.description: Optional: Specify the format to download. Possible values are `csv` or `logfile`. If omitted, defaults to `csv`. This request always downloads a ZIP file; this parameter only changes the format of the file contained within the ZIP.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

download_workflow_activity_log.title: Download Workflow Activity Log
download_workflow_activity_log.description: Download the daily log of workflow operations in your Vault. Learn more about Workflow Activity logs in Vault Help.

date.description: The date of the requested Workflow Activity log. Date is in UTC and follows the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. Cannot be more than 90 days in the past.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

get_email_notification_histories.title: Retrieve Email Notification Histories
get_email_notification_histories.description: Retrieve details about the email notifications sent by Vault. Details include the notification date, recipient, subject, and delivery status. In the UI, this information is available in Admin > Operations > Email Notification Status. Learn more about Email Notification Status in Vault Help.

start_date.description: Specify a start date to retrieve notification history. This date cannot be more than 3 months ago. To retrieve older email notifications, use the `all_dates` parameter instead. Dates must be in `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ` format. If time is omitted (`THH:mm:ssZ`), defaults to the start of the day. If `start_date` is omitted entirely, defaults to the start of the previous day. If you’ve specified a `start_date`, you must also specify an `end_date`.

end_date.description: Specify an end date to retrieve notification history. This date cannot be more than 30 days away from the specified `start_date`. Dates must be in `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ` format. If time is omitted (`THH:mm:ssZ`), defaults to the time of the API request. If you’ve specified an `end_date`, you must also specify a `start_date`.

all_dates.description: Set to `true` to request notification history for all dates. This request starts a job to prepare a downloadable `.zip` of CSV files of the entire notification history by year. This is similar to requesting Export Full History from the Vault UI. When requesting a full notification history, you must leave `start_date` and `end_date` blank and set `format_result` to `csv`. You can request an export of notification history for `all_dates` once every 24 hours.

format_result.description: To request a downloadable CSV file of your notification history, set this parameter to `csv`. The response contains a `jobId` to retrieve the job status, which provides a link to download the CSV file. If omitted, the API returns a JSON response with notification history and does not start a job. If `all_dates` is `true`, this parameter must be `csv`.

limit.description: Paginate the results by specifying the maximum number of histories per page in the response. This can be any value between `1` and `1000`. If omitted, defaults to `200`.

offset.description: Paginate the results displayed per page by specifying the amount of offset from the entry returned. If omitted, defaults to `0`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

delete_debug_log.description: Given a debug log ID, delete this debug log and all log files.

create_profiling_session.title: Create Profiling Session
create_profiling_session.description: Create a new SDK request profiling session. Profiling sessions allow developers to troubleshoot custom code and improve code quality by analyzing results at the SDK request level. Vault starts the profiling session immediately on creation. Profiling sessions run for either 20 minutes or up to 10,000 SDK requests, whichever comes first. To end a session early, use the End Profiling Session endpoint. Once ended, a session’s `status` is `processing__sys` while Vault prepares the data, which may take about 15 minutes. Once the `status` is `complete__sys`, the data is available for download with the Download Profiling Session Results endpoint.

label.description: The UI label for this request.

user_id.description: The user ID of the user to associate with this session. When specified, this SDK profiling session runs only for this user. If omitted, defaults to `null` which runs the session for all users.

description.description: An Admin-facing description of the session.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault starts the profiling session immediately and returns the session `id` and `name`.

delete_profiling_session.title: Delete Profiling Session
delete_profiling_session.description: Delete an inactive profiling session, which deletes the session and all data associated with the session. Inactive sessions have a `status` of `complete__sys`.

session_name.description: The `name` of the session, for example, `baseline__c`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the Vault deletes the specified profiling session and deletes all data associated with the session.

download_profiling_session_results.title: Download Profiling Session Results
download_profiling_session_results.description: Download the Profiler Log for a specific profiling session. A profiling session log is a CSV which contains one row for each SDK request, with a maximum of 100,000 rows.

session_name.description: The `name` of the session, for example, `baseline__c`.

output.description: The file's content, returned as the response body rather than as JSON.

end_profiling_session.title: End Profiling Session
end_profiling_session.description: Terminate a profiling session early. By default, profiling sessions run for either 20 minutes or up to 10,000 SDK requests, whichever comes first. Once ended, a session’s `status` is `processing__sys` while Vault prepares the data, which may take about 15 minutes. Once the `status` is `complete__sys`, the data is available for download with the Download Profiling Session Results endpoint.

session_name.description: The `name` of the session, for example, `baseline__c`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the Vault ends the profiling session. The session’s `status` becomes `processing__sys` while Vault prepares the data, which may take about 15 minutes.

create_vql_profiler_session.title: Create New Session
create_vql_profiler_session.description: Start a new VQL Query Profiler session. Only a single Profiler session can be active at a time.

label.description: Required label for the new session.

user_id.description: Captures queries for a specific initiating user. If omitted, includes all user queries.

query_origin.description: Captures queries coming from Vault API, Vault Java SDK, or both. Allowed values are `api`, `sdk`, `all`. If omitted, defaults to `all`.

query_targets.description: Captures queries for up to 20 query targets provided in a comma-separated list. If omitted, all query targets are included.

result_count_min.description: Captures queries with a minimum number of records returned. The minimum and default values are 0.

result_count_max.description: Captures queries with a maximum number of records returned. The maximum and default values are the configured limit for the Vault.

query_time_min.description: Captures queries with a minimum initial query execution time. If omitted, defaults to 0.

query_time_max.description: Captures queries with a maximum initial query execution time in seconds. If omitted, defaults to 1200.

response_status.description: Captures queries that have returned a specific response status. Allowed values are `all`, `warn`, `error`, `success`. If omitted, defaults to `all`.

description.description: Sets a string description of the session. Maximum 255 characters.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The response includes the following metadata, including any filters: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `id` | The ID of the new session. | | `name` | The name of the new session. |

list_vql_profiler_sessions.description: List All Sessions. Retrieve a list of all Query Profiler sessions.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The response includes the following metadata, including any filters: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `id` | The ID of this session. | | `label` | The label of this session. | | `name` | The name of this session.

get_vql_profiler_session.title: List Single Session
get_vql_profiler_session.description: Retrieve details for a specific Query Profiler session by name.

session_name.description: The name of the profiler session.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). The response includes the following metadata, including any filters: | Field Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `id` | The ID of this session. | | `label` | The label of this session. | | `name` | The name of this session.

delete_single_source_code_file.title: Delete Single Source Code File
delete_single_source_code_file.description: Delete a single source code file from the currently authenticated Vault. You cannot delete a code component currently in-use.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

disable_sdk_queue_delivery.title: Disable Delivery
disable_sdk_queue_delivery.description: The following endpoint allows you to disable the delivery of messages in an outbound Spark messaging queue, or an SDK job queue. This stop messages from exiting the queue. For example, disabling delivery on an SDK job queue stops messages from being delivered to the processor. This endpoint is not available for inbound Spark messaging queues. There is no way to stop received messages from processing in an inbound Spark queue.

queue_name.description: The name of a specific Queue.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

enable_sdk_queue_delivery.title: Enable Delivery
enable_sdk_queue_delivery.description: The following endpoint allows you to enable the delivery of messages in an outbound Spark messaging queue, or an SDK job queue. This allows messages to exit the queue. For example, enabling delivery on an SDK job queue allows messages to be delivered to the processor.

queue_name.description: The name of a specific Queue.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

reset_sdk_queue.title: Reset Queue
reset_sdk_queue.description: Delete all messages in a specific queue. This action is final and cannot be undone.

queue_name.description: The name of a specific queue.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

list_sdk_queues.title: Retrieve All Queues
list_sdk_queues.description: Retrieve All Queues. Retrieve all queues in a Vault. Calls GET /api/{version}/services/queues on the Vault API.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all available queues and their operational statuses.

get_sdk_queue_status.title: Retrieve Queue Status
get_sdk_queue_status.description: Retrieve Queue Status. Retrieve the status of a specific queue.

queue_name.description: The name of a specific queue. For example, `queue__c.`

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `delivery` | Indicates whether the delivery status is `enabled` or `disabled`. | | `messages_in_queue` | Displays the number of messages in the queue.

get_signing_certificate.title: Retrieve Signing Certificate
get_signing_certificate.description: The following endpoint allows you to retrieve a signing certificate included in a Spark message header to verify that the received message came from Vault. You do not need to authenticate your account prior to using this endpoint, as it does not require an `Authorization` HTTP request header.

cert_id.description: The `cert_id` is provided in each Spark message in the `X-VaultAPISignature-CertificateId` header.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the public key certificate (`.pem`) file used for Message Verification.

get_single_source_code_file.title: Retrieve Single Source Code File
get_single_source_code_file.description: Retrieve a single source code file from the currently authenticated Vault.

class_name.description: The fully qualified class name of your file.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

validate_imported_package.title: Validate Imported Package
validate_imported_package.description: Validate a previously imported VPK package with Vault Java SDK code. Note that this endpoint does not validate component dependencies for Configuration Migration packages.

package_id.description: The ID of the package to validate. You can find this in the API response of a package import, or in the URL of package in the Vault UI.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

cancel_raw_object_deployment.title: Cancel Raw Object Deployment
cancel_raw_object_deployment.description: Cancel a deployment of configuration changes to a raw object. To use this endpoint, your raw object `configuration_state` must be `IN_DEPLOYMENT`.

object_name.description: The name of the object on which to cancel deployment. This object’s `configuration_state` must be `IN_DEPLOYMENT`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). If the deployment is cancelled successfully, the API returns `SUCCESS`.

execute_mdl_script_asynchronously.title: Execute MDL Script Asynchronously
execute_mdl_script_asynchronously.description: This asynchronous endpoint executes the given MDL script on a Vault. While you can execute any MDL script with this endpoint, it is required if you’re operating on 10,000+ `raw` object records and executing one of the following operations: Enabling lifecycles Enabling or disabling object types Adding or removing a field Updating the max length of any variable-length field, such as Text, Long Text, or Rich Text Adding or removing an `Index` Changing the fields that compose an `Index` or otherwise would cause reindexing to occur After initiating this request, your raw object’s `configuration_state` becomes `IN_DEPLOYMENT`.

script.description: The MDL script to execute, sent as the raw request body. The body of the request should contain the MDL script to execute. Enter the body as raw data. The body must start with one of the following values: `CREATE` `RECREATE` `RENAME` `ALTER` `DROP` Learn more in the MDL Commands documentation.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `job_id` | The Job ID value to retrieve the status and results of this request. Use this ID to query for the job status and results.

get_asynchronous_mdl_script_results.title: Retrieve Asynchronous MDL Script Results
get_asynchronous_mdl_script_results.description: After submitting a request to deploy an MDL script asynchronously, you can query Vault to determine the results of the request. Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested a submission export job (via the API) which is no longer active. You must have a valid `job_id` field value returned from the Execute MDL Script Asynchronously request.

job_id.description: The `job_id` field value returned from the Execute MDL Script Asynchronously request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, this endpoint returns the results of the asynchronous MDL script execution, including any errors.

get_content_file.title: Retrieve Content File
get_content_file.description: Retrieve Content File. Retrieve the content file of a specified component.

component_type_and_record_name.description: The component type of the record followed by the name of the record from which to retrieve the content file. The format is `{Componenttype}.{record_name}`. For example, `Formattedoutput.my_formatted_output__c`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name__v` | The name of the file which can be used in MDL for referencing the component. | | `original_name__v` | The original name of the uploaded file.

upload_content_file.title: Upload Content File
upload_content_file.description: This endpoint allows you to upload a content file to be referenced by a component. Once uploaded, Vault stores the file in a generic files staging area where they will remain until referenced by a component. Once referenced, Vault cannot access the named file from the staging area.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name__v` | The name of the file which can be used in MDL for referencing the component. | | `format__v` | The format of the file.

execute_mdl_script.title: Execute MDL Script
execute_mdl_script.description: This synchronous endpoint executes the given MDL script on a Vault. Note that some large operations require use of the asynchronous endpoint.

script.description: The MDL script to execute, sent as the raw request body. The body of the request should contain the MDL script to execute. Enter the body as raw data. The body must start with one of the following values: `CREATE` `RECREATE` `RENAME` `ALTER` `DROP` Learn more in the MDL Commands documentation.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains details of the execute.

list_component_metadata.title: Retrieve All Component Metadata
list_component_metadata.description: Retrieve All Component Metadata. Retrieve metadata of all component types in your Vault.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response may include the following for each component type in the currently authenticated Vault: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `url` | URL to retrieve metadata for the component type.

get_component_record_collection.title: Retrieve Component Record Collection
get_component_record_collection.description: Retrieve all records for a specific component type. This endpoint does not support retrieving `Object` component records. Instead, use Retrieve Object Collection.

component_type.description: The component type name (`Picklist`, `Docfield`, `Doctype`, etc.). To retrieve records for `Object`, see Retrieve Object Collection.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains all component records in the Vault for the specified component type. Each component record returns a minimum of API `name` and UI `label`, but most types return more.

get_component_record_mdl.title: Retrieve Component Record (MDL)
get_component_record_mdl.description: Retrieve metadata of a specific component record as MDL. To retrieve as JSON or XML, see Retrieve Component Record. Vault does not generate RECREATE statements for all component types. For details, see the Generate RECREATE row of the Supported Operations table in the Component Type Reference.

component_type_and_record_name.description: The component type name (`Picklist`, `Docfield`, `Doctype`, etc.) followed by the name of the record from which to retrieve metadata. The format is `{Componenttype}.{record_name}`. For example, `Picklist.color__c`. Find this with the Retrieve Component Record Collection endpoint.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains a RECREATE MDL statement of metadata for the specified component record. Metadata returned varies based on component type. If a field returns as blank, it means the record currently has no value for that field.

get_component_record.title: Retrieve Component Record (XML/JSON)
get_component_record.description: Retrieve metadata of a specific component record as JSON or XML. To retrieve as MDL, see Retrieve Component Record MDL. Not all component types are eligible for record description retrieval. For details, see the Describe row of the Supported Operations table in the Component Type Reference.

component_type_and_record_name.description: The component type name (`Picklist`, `Docfield`, `Doctype`, etc.) followed by the name of the record from which to retrieve metadata. The format is `{Componenttype}.{record_name}`. For example, `Picklist.color__c`. Find this with the Retrieve Component Record Collection endpoint.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings or Label Sets are available, retrieve them by setting `loc` to `true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains the complete definition for a specific component record. If a field returns as blank or null, it means the record has no value for that field.

get_component_type_metadata.title: Retrieve Component Type Metadata
get_component_type_metadata.description: Retrieve Component Type Metadata. Retrieve metadata of a specific component type.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response contains metadata for the specified component type. Metadata returned varies for each component and subcomponent type. See Vault Components for more information. Note that some attributes return a `default_cap` value.

initiate_multi_record_workflow.title: Initiate Multi-Record Workflow
initiate_multi_record_workflow.description: Initiate a multi-record workflow on a set of records. If any record is not in the relevant state or does not meet configured field conditions, the API returns `INVALID_DATA` for the invalid records and the workflow does not start.

contents_sys.description: Input a comma-separated list of records, in the format `Object:{objectname}.{record_ID}`. For example, `Object:product__c.V3O000000005001`. Maximum 100 records.

description_sys.description: Description of the workflow. Maximum 128 characters.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `record_id__v` | The `id` value of the `envelope__sys` record. | | `workflow_id` | The workflow `id` field value. |

list_multi_record_workflows.title: Retrieve All Multi-Record Workflows
list_multi_record_workflows.description: Retrieve all available multi-record workflows which: The authenticated user has permissions to view or initiate Can be initiated through the API

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The workflow name. | | `label` | UI label for the workflow. | | `type` | Type of workflow.

get_multi_record_workflow_details.title: Retrieve Multi-Record Workflow Details
get_multi_record_workflow_details.description: Retrieves the fields required to initiate a specific multi-record workflow.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists the fields that must be configured with values in order to initiate the workflow. These are based on the controls configured in the workflow start step.

initiate_object_action_on_single_record.title: Initiate Object Action on a Single Record
initiate_object_action_on_single_record.description: Use this request to initiate an action on a specific object record.

object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value.

object_record_id.description: The object record `id` field value from which to retrieve user actions.

action_name.description: The name of the `Objectaction` or `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction` to initiate. You can retrieve this from the Retrieve User Actions request. The format for `action_name` is `Objectaction.{vobject}.{action}` or `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction.{vobject}.{state}.{action}`. For example, `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction.country__v.active_state__c.start_wf_useraction__c`.

story_event_key.description: The ID of the target Story Event object record when executing the Apply Milestone Template action. This is only applicable in Clinical Operations Vaults.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

initiate_object_action_on_multiple_recor.title: Initiate Object Action on Multiple Records
initiate_object_action_on_multiple_recor.description: Use this request to initiate an object user action on multiple records. Maximum 500 records per batch.

object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value.

action_name.description: The name of the `Objectaction` or `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction` to initiate. This is obtained from the Retrieve User Actions request. The format for `action_name` is `Objectaction.{vobject}.{action}` or `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction.{vobject}.{state}.{action}`. For example, `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction.country__v.active_state__c.start_wf_useraction__c`.

ids.description: Comma-separated list of object record ids on which to initiate the action.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_object_record_user_actions.title: Retrieve Object Record User Actions
get_object_record_user_actions.description: Retrieve all available user actions that can be initiated on a specific object record which: The authenticated user has permissions to view or initiate Can be initiated through the API

object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value.

loc.description: Optional: When `true`, retrieves localized (translated) strings for the `label`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all available user actions that can be initiated on the specified object record. For users with the View permission, the response includes a link to retrieve the metadata for the specified user action.

get_object_user_action_details.title: Retrieve Object User Action Details
get_object_user_action_details.description: Once you've retrieved the available user actions, use this request to retrieve the details for a specific user action.

object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value.

object_record_id.description: The object record `id` field value from which to retrieve user action details.

action_name.description: Either the name of the `Objectaction` or `Objectlifecyclestateuseraction` to initiate. This is obtained from the Retrieve User Actions request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response returns metadata for the specified object action. For users with the View permission, the response includes a link to retrieve the metadata for the specified user action.

create_picklist_values.title: Create Picklist Values
create_picklist_values.description: Add new values to a picklist. Learn about picklist limits in Vault Help.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the body. In the body of the request, use `value_1`, `value_2`, etc., set to alphanumeric values. Enter each new picklist value `label` as they will be displayed in the UI. You do not need to enter a `name` value, instead, Vault uses the `label` to create the picklist value `name`. You cannot specify picklist order on creation. New picklist values are added in the order they are submitted, after any existing values in the picklist. To re-order picklist values, use the Vault UI or Vault Toolbox.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). | Metadata Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The picklist value name. This is used to reference this value in the API, and displayed to Vault Admins in the UI. | | `label` | The picklist value label.

inactivate_picklist_value.title: Inactivate Picklist Value
inactivate_picklist_value.description: Inactivate a value from a picklist. This does not affect picklist values that are already in use.

picklist_value_name.description: The picklist value `name` field value (`north_america__c`, `south_america__c`, etc.)

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

list_picklists.title: Retrieve All Picklists
list_picklists.description: Retrieve all picklists in the authenticated Vault which the authenticated user has access to view.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings or Label Sets are available, retrieve them by setting `loc` to `true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). | Metadata Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | Picklist name. This is used only in the API and displayed in the Admin UI. | | `label` | Picklist label. This is used in the API and UI. Users see the label on document and object picklist fields.

get_picklist_values.title: Retrieve Picklist Values
get_picklist_values.description: Retrieve Picklist Values. Retrieve all active values configured on a picklist.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings or Label Sets are available, retrieve them by setting `loc` to `true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response returns the active values on a picklist in ascending order, designated by the picklist value's `order` attribute.

update_picklist_value_label.title: Update Picklist Value Label
update_picklist_value_label.description: Change a picklist value `label` (only). To change a picklist value `name`, see Update Picklist Value. Use caution when editing picklist labels or names. When these attributes are changed, they affect all existing document and object metadata that refer to the picklist. For users in the UI who are accustomed to seeing a particular selection, the changes may cause confusion. This may also break existing integrations that access picklist values via the API.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body. To change an existing picklist value `label`, use its picklist value `name` set to a new label. The picklist value `name` will remain unchanged. For example, to change the label of the existing `"north_america__c=North America"`, enter `"north_america__c=North America/United States"`. You may include one or more picklist values in the request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). As shown above, only the picklist value `label` has changed. The picklist value `name` remains the same. The new label will be automatically updated on all documents and objects in which it is used.

update_picklist_value.title: Update Picklist Value
update_picklist_value.description: Change a picklist value `name` or `status`. To change a picklist value `label`, see Update Picklist Value Label. Use caution when editing picklist value names. When you change a picklist value name, it may affect existing document and object metadata that refer to the picklist. This may also break existing integrations that access picklist values via the API.

picklist_value_name.description: The picklist value `name` field value (`north_america__c`, `south_america__c`, etc.)

name.description: Conditional. The new name for a picklist value. This does not affect the label. Vault adds `__c` after processing. Special characters and double underscores `__` are not allowed.

status.description: Conditional. The new status for a picklist value. Valid values are `active` or `inactive`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Only the picklist value `name` is changed. The picklist value `label` remains the same. In the UI, Admins will see the new name in Business Admin > Picklists > {Picklist}.

change_sandbox_size.title: Change Sandbox Size
change_sandbox_size.description: Change the size of a sandbox Vault for the authenticated Vault. You can initiate this action if there are sufficient allowances and the current sandbox meets the data and user limits of the requested size. Learn more about sandbox sizes in Vault Help.

name.description: The name of the sandbox Vault.

size.description: The requested size of the sandbox: `Small`, `Medium`, `Large`, `Very Large`, `Extra Large`, or `Full`. Learn more about sandbox sizes and their limits in Vault Help.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the `responseStatus` and lists any errors encountered.

create_or_refresh_sandbox.title: Create or Refresh Sandbox
create_or_refresh_sandbox.description: Create a new sandbox for the currently authenticated Vault. Include the `source_snapshot` parameter in the request body to create a new sandbox from an existing snapshot. Providing a name which already exists will refresh the existing sandbox Vault. You can also refresh a sandbox from a snapshot.

source.description: The source to refresh the sandbox from: `vault`; `snapshot`

source_snapshot.description: If the source is a `snapshot`, provide the `api_name` of the snapshot to create the sandbox from. You can obtain the `api_name` using the Retrieve Sandbox Snapshots request.

type.description: The type of sandbox, such as `config`.

size.description: The size of the sandbox: `Small`, `Medium`, `Large`, `Very Large`, `Extra Large`, or `Full`. Learn more about sandbox sizes and their limits in Vault Help.

domain.description: The domain to use for the new sandbox. Must be a valid domain. You can retrieve valid domains from the Retrieve Domains endpoint. Only domains of `type: Sandbox` are allowed. Must be lower-case, and must include the domain extension.

name.description: The name of the sandbox Vault, which appears on the My Vaults page. Providing a new name creates a new sandbox, whereas providing an existing name refreshes the existing sandbox. How often you can refresh a Vault depends on its size. Learn more about refreshing sandboxes in Vault Help.

add_requester.description: This boolean field adds the currently authenticated user as a Vault Owner in the new sandbox. If set to `false,` the Domain Admin users in the sandbox domain will become Vault Owners in the sandbox Vault. If omitted, defaults to `true`.

release.description: The type of release. This can be `general`, `limited`, or `prerelease`. If omitted, defaults to the release level of the source Vault. Learn more about Vault releases in Vault Help.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `job_id` | The Job ID value to retrieve the status and results of the sandbox creation request.

delete_sandbox.title: Delete Sandbox
delete_sandbox.description: Delete a sandbox Vault. How often you can delete a Vault depends on its size. Learn more about deleting sandboxes in Vault Help.

name.description: The `name` of the sandbox Vault to delete. This is the name which appears on the My Vaults page.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

generate_api_access_token_for_sandbox.title: Generate API Access Token for Sandbox
generate_api_access_token_for_sandbox.description: Generate an API access token for a sandbox Vault. Tokens are preserved upon refreshing a sandbox. Learn more about generating access tokens and how they are retained when managing sandboxes.

sandbox_name.description: The name of the sandbox Vault to create the access token for. This is the name which appears on the My Vaults page.

name_v.description: The name or description of the access token.

expiry_date_v.description: The expiration date of the access token, in `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` format. Dates and times are in UTC. If the time is not specified, it will default to before midnight (`23:59:59`) in the user's timezone on the specified date. The maximum expiration period may vary based on the user's security profile. If allowed by the user's security profile, this parameter can be omitted to indicate the access token never expires.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, this request returns the `id` for the access token as well as its value (`token__sys`). The access token's value is only visible upon creation and should be stored safely.

build_production_vault.title: Build Production Vault
build_production_vault.description: Given a pre-production Vault, build a production Vault. This is analogous to the Build action in the Vault UI. After building your Vault, you can promote it to production. You can build or rebuild the source Vault for a given pre-production Vault no more than three times in a 24 hour period.
