object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value (`product__v`, `country__v`, `custom_object__c`, etc.).

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all fields and values configured on the object record. When Custom Sharing Rules have been enabled on the object (`"dynamic_security": true`), the response includes the following additional information: `manually_assigned_shari…

get_object_records.title: Retrieve Object Records
get_object_records.description: To retrieve all records for a specific Vault object, use VQL or the Direct Data API. For example, the following VQL query will retrieve all records for a specific object:

q.description: `SELECT id, name__v FROM {object_name}` where `{object_name}` is the `name__v` field value of the object to retrieve records.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_results_of_cascade_delete_job.title: Retrieve Results of Cascade Delete Job
get_results_of_cascade_delete_job.description: After submitting a request to cascade delete an object record, you can query Vault to determine the results of the request. Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested a cascade delete job (via the API) which is no longer active. You must have a valid `job_id value`, retrieved from the response of the cascade delete request.

object_name.description: The name of the object which was deleted.

job_status.description: Possible values are `success` or `failure`. Find if your job succeeded or failed by retrieving the job status.

job_id.description: The ID of the job, retrieved from the response of the job request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_results_of_deep_copy_job.title: Retrieve Results of Deep Copy Job
get_results_of_deep_copy_job.description: After submitting a request to deep copy an object record, you can query Vault to determine the results of the request. Before submitting this request: You must have previously requested a deep copy job (via the API) which is no longer active. You must have a valid `job_id` value, retrieved from the response of the deep copy request.

object_name.description: The name of the deep copied object.

job_status.description: Possible values are `success` or `failure`. Find if your job succeeded or failed by retrieving the job status.

job_id.description: The ID of the job, retrieved from the response of the job request.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

recalculate_roll_up_fields.title: Recalculate Roll-up Fields
recalculate_roll_up_fields.description: Recalculate all Roll-up fields for the specified object. Learn more about Roll-up fields in Vault Help. When performing a full recalculation, Vault evaluates all Roll-up fields on an object asynchronously. This endpoint is equivalent to the Recalculate Roll-up Fields action in the Vault UI. While a recalculation is running, Admins cannot start another recalculation using either Vault API or Vault UI.

object_name.description: The name of the object on which to start the Roll-up field recalculation.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Returns `SUCCESS` if the recalculation starts successfully, or `FAILURE` if a recalculation is already running for the specified object.

get_roll_up_field_recalculation_status.title: Retrieve Roll-up Field Recalculation Status
get_roll_up_field_recalculation_status.description: Determine whether a Roll-up field recalculation is currently running. Learn more about Roll-up fields in Vault Help.

object_name.description: The name of the object for which to check the status of a Roll-up field recalculation.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response specifies the status of the Roll-up field recalculation as either `RUNNING` or `NOT_RUNNING`.

update_corporate_currency_fields.title: Update Corporate Currency Fields
update_corporate_currency_fields.description: Currency is a field type available on all Vault objects. Whenever a user populates a local currency field value, Vault automatically populates the related corporate currency field value, except in the following scenarios: Admins change the Corporate Currency setting for the vault Admins update the Rate setting for the local currency used by a record This endpoint updates the `field_corp__sys` field values of an object record based on the Rate of the currency, denoted by the `local_currency__sys` field of the specified record. Learn more about Currency Fields in Vault Help.

object_name.description: The object `name__v` field value, for example, `product__v`.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: id: The object record `id` field value. If you don't provide an `id`, Vault updates corporate fields of all record…

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

update_object_records.title: Update Object Records
update_object_records.description: Update Object Records in bulk. You can use this endpoint to update user records (`user__sys`). The maximum input size is 50 MB. The values in the input must be UTF-8 encoded. CSVs must follow the standard RFC 4180 format, with some exceptions. Vault removes XML characters that fall outside of the character range from the request body. The maximum batch size is 500.

object_name.description: The name of the object, for example, `product__v`.

id_param.description: Optional: To identify objects in your input by a unique field, add `idParam={field_name}` to the request endpoint. You can use any object field that has `unique` set to `true` in the object metadata. For example, `idParam=external_id__v`.

migration_mode.description: If set to `true`, Vault allows you to update object records in a noninitial state and with minimal validation, create inactive records, and set standard and system-managed fields such as `created_by__v`. Does not bypass record triggers. You must have the Record Migration permission to use this header. Learn more about Record Migration Mode in Vault Help.

no_triggers.description: If set to `true` and Record Migration Mode is enabled, it bypasses all system, standard, custom SDK triggers, and Action Triggers. Before using this parameter, learn more about bypassing triggers.

records.description: The records to send, as a JSON array of objects. Fields per record: id (required): The object record ID. You can only update an object record ID once per request.; field_name: The field name to update on this object record. Use the Object Metadata API to retrieve all fields configured…; state__v: Specifies the lifecycle state of the record when `X-VaultAPI-MigrationMode` is set to `true`.; state_label: Specifies the lifecycle state type of the record when `X-VaultAPI-MigrationMode` is set to `true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Vault returns a `responseStatus` for the request: `SUCCESS`: This request executed with no warnings. Individual records may be failures. `WARNING`: This request executed with at least one warning on an individual record.

run_vql_query.title: Submitting a Query
run_vql_query.description: Submitting a Query. Retrieve and filter Vault data using a VQL query.

describe_query.description: Set to `true` to include static field metadata in the response for the data record. If not specified, the response does not include any static field metadata. This option eliminates the need to make additional API calls to understand the shape of query response data.

record_properties.description: Optional: If present, the response includes the record properties object. Possible values are `all`, `hidden`, `redacted`, and `weblink`. If omitted, the record properties object is not included in the response.

document_properties.description: Optional: If present, the response includes the document properties object. The only possible value is `all`. If omitted, the document properties object is not included in the response.

q.description: A VQL query of up to 50,000 characters, formatted as `q={query}`. For example, `q=SELECT id FROM documents`. Note that submitting the query as a query parameter instead may cause you to exceed the maximum URL length.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response includes the following information: | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `pagesize` | The number of records displayed per page. This can be modified. Learn more.

initiate_workflow_actions_on_multiple_wo.title: Initiate Workflow Actions on Multiple Workflows
initiate_workflow_actions_on_multiple_wo.description: Use this request to initiate a workflow action on multiple workflows. This starts an asynchronous job whose status you can check with the Retrieve Job Status endpoint. Maximum 500 workflows per request.

action.description: The `name` of the workflow action. To get this value, Retrieve Bulk Workflow Actions.

workflow_ids.description: Input a comma-separated list of `workflow_id__v` field values. Maximum 500 workflows.

cancellation_comment.description: If this workflow requires a comment for cancellation, use this parameter to provide a comment.

current_task_assignee.description: Input the user ID of the user whose tasks you wish to reassign. You cannot reassign specific tasks for a user, only all tasks currently assigned to a user.

new_task_assignee.description: Input the user ID of the user who will receive the newly assigned tasks.

user_ids.description: Conditional. To cancel tasks by user ID, input a comma-separated list of the user IDs for the users whose tasks you wish to cancel. You cannot cancel specific tasks for a user, only all tasks currently assigned to a user. Maximum 100 user IDs per request.

task_ids.description: Conditional. To cancel tasks by task ID, input a comma-separated list of the task IDs to cancel. You cannot cancel task IDs for a specific user, only all instances of the given task IDs.

new_workflow_owner.description: Input the ID of the user who will become the new workflow owner. For example, `54937`.

current_workflow_owner.description: Input the ID of the user who is the current workflow owner. For example, `87944`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response returns the `job_id` for the action, and the authenticated user will receive an email notification with details of any failures that occur.

get_bulk_workflow_action_details.title: Retrieve Bulk Workflow Action Details
get_bulk_workflow_action_details.description: Once you’ve retrieved the available workflow actions, use this request to retrieve the details for a specific workflow action.

action.description: The `name` of the workflow action. To get this value, Retrieve Bulk Workflow Actions.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response returns metadata for the specified workflow action, including the fields required to execute the action.

get_bulk_workflow_actions.title: Retrieve Bulk Workflow Actions
get_bulk_workflow_actions.description: Retrieve all available workflow actions that can be initiated on a workflow which: The authenticated user has permissions to view or initiate Can be initiated through the API

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all available workflow actions for a Vault. | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | `name` | The workflow action name. | | `label` | The workflow action label as seen in the UI. |

complete_job_step.title: Complete Job Step
complete_job_step.description: Accepts a request to complete a Job step. You must have the Workflow: Complete Job Step permission. Learn more about Workflow Job steps in Vault Help.

completion_status_sys.description: The completion status verdict required to complete the Job step. Valid values are: `success__sys`; `errors_encountered__sys`; `failed__sys`

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

initiate_workflow_action.title: Initiate Workflow Action
initiate_workflow_action.description: Initiate Workflow Action. Initiate a workflow action on a specific workflow.

workflow_action.description: The workflow action name retrieved from Retrieve Workflow Actions.

new_workflow_owner.description: The `id` of the user who will become the new workflow owner, in the format `user:{id}`. For example, `user:6014`.

email_recipients.description: A comma-delimited list of email recipients or groups, in the format `user:{user_id}` and `group:{group_label}`. For example, `user:1082,user:4802,group:incompleteTaskOwners,user:3582`. To find available `{group_label}`s, Retrieve Workflow Action Details for `emailparticipants`. If a user is not a potential recipient based on their task status, the user will not receive an email.

email_message.description: The body of the email message to send to users. Maximum 5,000 characters.

send_copy_to_self.description: Set to `true` to send a copy of the email to the authenticated user. If omitted, defaults to `false`.

participants.description: The `id` of the user to add as a participant, in the format `user:{id}`. For example, `user:1006`.

contents_sys.description: The `id` of the document to remove from the workflow. To remove multiple documents, use a comma-separated list of `id`s.

workflow_due_date.description: The new due date for the workflow, in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). If the `{workflow_action}` executes successfully, the response returns `SUCCESS`. For example, the `cancel` workflow action. On `FAILURE`, the response returns an error `type` and `message` describing the reason for the failure.

get_workflow_action_details.title: Retrieve Workflow Action Details
get_workflow_action_details.description: Retrieve details about a workflow action. For example, the `prompts` needed to complete a workflow action.

workflow_action.description: The `name` of the workflow action. To get this value, you can Retrieve Workflow Actions.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all prompts required to complete the workflow action. If the workflow action does not require any prompts, the response will only list SUCCESS.

get_workflow_actions.title: Retrieve Workflow Actions
get_workflow_actions.description: Retrieve all available workflow actions that can be initiated on a specific workflow.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all available workflow actions. Each action includes the following fields: `name` - The workflow action name used to initiate the workflow in the request. `label` - The workflow action label as seen in the UI.

get_workflow_details.title: Retrieve Workflow Details
get_workflow_details.description: Retrieve Workflow Details. Retrieve the details for a specific workflow.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists the workflow details. The workflow may include the following fields: `id` - The workflow ID. `label__v` - The workflow label as seen in the UI. `status__v` - The current status of the workflow.

get_workflows.title: Retrieve Workflows
get_workflows.description: Retrieve all current, cancelled, and completed workflow instances for a specific object record or all workflows available to a particular workflow participant.

object_v.description: To retrieve all workflows configured on an object, include the Vault object `name__v` and object record `id` field values as `object__v={name__v}&record_id__v={id}`. These two parameters are required when the `participant` parameter is not used.

participant.description: To retrieve all workflows available to a particular user, include the user `id` field value as `participant={id}`. To retrieve your own workflows, set this value to `participant=me()`. This parameter is required when the `object__v` and `record_id__v` parameters are not used.

status_v.description: To retrieve all workflows with specific statuses, include one or more status `name__v` field values. For example: `status__v=active__v`, `status__v=active__v,completed__v`. Workflows with `status__v=active__v` are in progress for the indicated object record. Valid statuses include: `active__v`; `completed__v`; `cancelled__v`

offset.description: This parameter is used to paginate the results. It specifies the amount of offset from the first record returned. Vault returns 200 records per page by default. If you are viewing the first 200 results (page 1) and want to see the next page, set this to `offset=201`.

page_size.description: This parameter is used to paginate the results. It specifies the size number of records to display per page. Vault returns 200 records per page by default. You can set this value lower or as high as 1000 records per page. For example: `page_size=1000`.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all workflows matching the query parameters. Each workflow may include the following fields: `id` - The workflow ID. `label__v` - The workflow label as seen in the UI. `status__v` - The current status of the workflow.

accept_multi_item_workflow_task.title: Accept Multi-item Workflow Task
accept_multi_item_workflow_task.description: Accept an available task for a multi-record workflow. If the task is available to multiple users, any one of the assigned users can accept the task. To undo your acceptance of an available workflow task, use Undo Workflow Task Acceptance. Vault may prevent you from accepting a task if you've already accepted, assigned, or completed another task, or have a restricted role.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault accepts the available workflow task on behalf of the authenticated user.

accept_single_record_workflow_task.title: Accept Single Record Workflow Task
accept_single_record_workflow_task.description: Accept an available task for a workflow configured for a single record. If the task is available to multiple users, any one of the assigned users can accept the task. To undo your acceptance of an available workflow task, use Undo Workflow Task Acceptance. Vault may prevent you from accepting a task if you've already accepted, assigned, or completed another task, or have a restricted role.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault accepts the available workflow task on behalf of the authenticated user.

cancel_workflow_task.title: Cancel Workflow Task
cancel_workflow_task.description: Cancel an open workflow task. This endpoint supports single and multi-record workflows.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Returns `SUCCESS` if the task was canceled successfully.

complete_multi_item_workflow_task.title: Complete Multi-item Workflow Task
complete_multi_item_workflow_task.description: Complete an open workflow task for a multi-item workflow. This endpoint does not support initiating task actions requiring eSignatures (where `esignature` is `true`). To provide multiple verdicts for items without completing an open workflow task, use Manage Multi-item Workflow Content.

verdict_public_key_c.description: Conditional. The verdict name. Retrieve possible verdict `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

reason_c.description: Conditional. The reason name. Retrieve possible reason `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

capacity_c.description: Conditional. The capacity name. Retrieve possible capacity `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault completes the workflow task on behalf of the authenticated user.

complete_single_record_workflow_task.title: Complete Single Record Workflow Task
complete_single_record_workflow_task.description: Complete an open workflow task for a workflow configured for a single record. This endpoint does not support initiating task actions requiring eSignatures (where `esignature` is `true`).

verdict_public_key_c.description: Conditional. The verdict name. Retrieve possible verdict `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

reason_c.description: Conditional. The reason name. Retrieve possible reason `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

capacity_c.description: Conditional. The capacity name. Retrieve possible capacity `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault completes the workflow task on behalf of the authenticated user.

manage_multi_item_workflow_content.title: Manage Multi-item Workflow Content
manage_multi_item_workflow_content.description: Manage content in a multi-item workflow without completing an open workflow task. For example, you can use this endpoint to provide verdicts for specific items without completing the task. This endpoint does not support initiating task actions requiring eSignatures (where `esignature` is `true`).

verdict_public_key_c.description: Conditional. The verdict name. Retrieve possible verdict `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

reason_c.description: Conditional. The reason name. Retrieve possible reason `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

capacity_c.description: Conditional. The capacity name. Retrieve possible capacity `name` values by sending a request to Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault modifies the contents in the multi-item workflow according to the JSON payload provided. Use Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details to confirm any changes to `current_values`.

reassign_multi_item_workflow_task.title: Reassign Multi-item Workflow Task
reassign_multi_item_workflow_task.description: Reassign an open workflow task to another user for a multi-item workflow. You cannot reassign a task to a user who is already assigned to that specific task, has completed that task, or is configured with a restricted role. However, you can reassign a user to continuing iterations of the same task if an Admin has enabled users in the workflow to only complete one task.

task_id.description: The `id` of the task to reassign.

task_assignee_v.description: The `id` of the user who will become the new task assignee, in the format `user:{id}`. For example, `user:100307`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Returns `SUCCESS` if the task was successfully reassigned. Vault notifies the new task owner and the previous task owner of the reassignment.

reassign_single_record_workflow_task.title: Reassign Single Record Workflow Task
reassign_single_record_workflow_task.description: Reassign an open workflow task to another user for a workflow configured for a single record. You cannot reassign a task to a user who is already assigned to that specific task, has completed that task, or is configured with a restricted role. However, you can reassign a user to continuing iterations of the same task if an Admin has enabled users in the workflow to only complete one task.

task_id.description: The `id` of the task to reassign.

task_assignee_v.description: The `id` of the user who will become the new task assignee, in the format `user:{id}`. For example, `user:100307`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Returns `SUCCESS` if the task was successfully reassigned. Vault notifies the new task owner and the previous task owner of the reassignment.

get_workflow_task_action_details.title: Retrieve Workflow Task Action Details
get_workflow_task_action_details.description: Retrieve the details of a specific workflow task action. The response lists the details of the task action, including all fields required to initiate the action. Note that task actions where `esignature` is `true` cannot be initiated via the API.

task_action.description: The name of the task action retrieved from Retrieve Workflow Task Actions.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_workflow_task_actions.title: Retrieve Workflow Task Actions
get_workflow_task_actions.description: Retrieve all available actions that can be initiated on a given workflow task.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array).

get_workflow_task_details.title: Retrieve Workflow Task Details
get_workflow_task_details.description: Retrieve Workflow Task Details. Retrieve the details of a specific workflow task.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all workflow tasks matching the query parameters. The task may include the following fields: `id` - The task ID. `label__v` - The task label as seen in the UI. `status__v` - The current status of the task.

get_workflow_tasks.title: Retrieve Workflow Tasks
get_workflow_tasks.description: Retrieve Workflow Tasks. Retrieve all available tasks across all workflows.

object_v.description: To retrieve all workflow tasks configured on an object, include the Vault object `name__v` and object record `id` field values as `object__v={name__v}&record_id__v={id}`. These two parameters are required when the `assignee__v` parameter is not used.

assignee_v.description: To retrieve all workflow tasks available to a particular user, include the user `id` field value as `assignee__v={id}`. To retrieve your own workflow tasks, set this value to `assignee__v=me()`. This parameter is required when the `object__v` and `record_id__v` parameters are not used.

status_v.description: To retrieve all workflow tasks with specific statuses, include one or more status `name__v` field values. For example: `status__v=available__v` or `status__v=available__v,completed__v`.

offset.description: This parameter is used to paginate the results. It specifies the amount of offset from the first record returned. Vault returns 200 records per page by default. If you are viewing the first 200 results (page 1) and want to see the next page, set this to `offset=201`.

page_size.description: This parameter is used to paginate the results. It specifies the size number of records to display per page. Vault returns 200 records per page by default. You can set this value lower or as high as 1000 records per page. For example: `page_size=1000`.

loc.description: When localized (translated) strings are available, retrieve them by including `loc=true`.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, the response lists all workflow tasks matching the query parameters. Each task may include the following fields: `id` - The task ID. `label__v` - The task label as seen in the UI. `status__v` - The current status of the task.

undo_workflow_task_acceptance.title: Undo Workflow Task Acceptance
undo_workflow_task_acceptance.description: Undo your acceptance of an available workflow task. Once released, the task is available again to any of the assigned users. This endpoint supports single and multi-item workflows.

fields.description: Name/value pairs to send in the request body.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). On `SUCCESS`, Vault reeases the available workflow task on behalf of the authenticated user. The task is available again to any of the assigned users.

update_workflow_task_due_date.title: Update Workflow Task Due Date
update_workflow_task_due_date.description: Update the due date of an assigned workflow task. This endpoint supports single and multi-item workflows. If the workflow is configured to set all task due dates to the workflow due date, updates to individual task due dates will not affect the overall workflow due date. You cannot update task due dates that are configured to sync with an object or document field.

task_due_date_v.description: The new due date for the task, in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. The new task due date cannot be the same as the current task due date.

output.description: Vault's JSON reply. `responseStatus` is SUCCESS, WARNING or FAILURE (failures come back with HTTP 200 and an `errors` array). Returns `SUCCESS` if the due date was successfully updated. Vault notifies the task owner of the new due date.
